 Judgment

This appeal by the Insurance Company is directed against the judgment and award dated 04/09/2018, passed in MVC No.2887/2015, by the learned XVIII Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes and Member, MACT, Bengaluru (SCCH-4), whereby, compensation of Rs.4,87,000/- and also interest at 6% p.a. on Rs.4,62,000/- from the date of petition till its realization has been awarded by the Tribunal.
2.

entities.text: XVIII Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes and Member, MACT, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner Master Chandan represented by his father/guardian, has filed a claim petition before the NC: 2023:KHC:40585 Tribunal claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

3. It is the case of the guardian, father of the petitioner that on 18.02.2015 at about 7.00 p.m., while his son Chandan was standing in front of his house, at Yellamma Temple Road, Bandepalya, the driver of the Mahindra Max pickup goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-08- 6167 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to which, his son sustained various fractures to the right leg and whole body.

Immediately he was shifted to Ashwad Hospital for first aid and later,
shifted to Sagar Hospital, wherein, he underwent surgery and incurred expenses of Rs.5,00,000/-
towards medical, food, nourishment and other incidental expenses.

It was further contended that,
his son Chandan is a brilliant student, was active in sports and due to the accident, his education and sports activities were seriously affected.

It was contended that, the accident took place due to the negligence of the driver of the Mahindra Max pickup goods NC: 2023:KHC:40585 vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-6167 and Madiwala Traffic Police have registered the case in Cr.No.31/2015 under Sections 279 and 337 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
4. In pursuance of the notice issued by the Tribunal, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through their counsel and filed written statement.

sentences.text:
The respondent No.1 in his written statement denied the petition averments and contended that,
on 18.02.2015, he was the driver-cum-owner of the Mahindra Max pickup goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-6167 and the same was driven carefully towards the left side of the road and the minor petitioner suddenly come on the road without seeing any side of the road and though he made attempt to control the vehicle, but the vehicle slowly touched him and he sustained simple injuries.
The accident NC: 2023:KHC:40585 took place due to the negligence of the petitioner.

It was further contended that the said vehicle is duly insured with the respondent No.2 and the same is in force as on the date of the accident and he is having valid and effective driving licence and insurance and hence, he is not liable to pay compensation and prayed to dismiss the petition.
6.

The respondent No.2-Insurance Company in its written statement has admitted the issuance of policy in favour of the respondent No.1 in respect of Mahindra Max pickup goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-6167 and contends that liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
The driver of insured vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and as such, the insured has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it was contended that, the insured vehicle is falsely implicated by the petitioner colluding with the insured and police.

The accident in question did take place due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner alone, as on the date of incident the NC: 2023:KHC:40585 petitioner was well aware of that the Bolero goods vehicle driver was taking reverse and the driver was driving very slowly and cautious manner, the petitioner suddenly entered the road and came between the Bolero goods vehicle and tried to cross the road with out having proper look out of traffic in a negligent and careless manner;
hence, the accident did take place due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner alone; the compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant and fanciful.
Hence, he prayed to dismiss the petition.

7. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed appropriate issues and natural guardian/father of the petitioner was examined as PW.1 and he has examined one witness as PW.2 and Exs.P1 to P24 were marked in evidence.

Respondents have examined four witnesses as RWs.1 to 4 and got marked Exs.R1 to R4.
8.

The Tribunal after hearing both the sides and considering the material available on record has awarded NC: 2023:KHC:40585 the compensation of Rs.4,87,000/- under different heads and directed the insurance company to deposit the same as below:
AMOUNT PARTICULARS (IN RS.)

Pain and sufferings 40,000/-
 Medical Expenses 2,37,000/-
 Loss of earning of father of petitioner 40,000/-
 during the period of treatment  Disability 1,00,000/-
 Towards food, nourishment and 15,000/-
 attendant charges
Towards loss of amenities 30,000/-

Towards future medical expenses 25,000/-
 TOTAL 4,87,000/-

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the Insurance Company is before this Court in appeal.
10. On issuance of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsels and on admitting the appeal, the Tribunal records have been secured.

11. Heard Sri Ravi S. Samprathi, learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company, Sri.H.C.Shivaramu, NC: 2023:KHC:40585 learned counsel for respondent No.1 and Sri.Bharath L., learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the Tribunal records.
12.

Learned counsel appearing for the appellant/Insurance Company submit that initially the medical records showed an accident said to have committed by a tractor but however, the medical records were later manipulated and it was shown that the accident occurred involving the Mahindra Max pickup goods vehicle bearing KA-08-6167.
Further, he submitted that there is a delay of 1 day in filing the complaint and therefore, he alleged offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the case.
It is contended that the petitioner and respondent No.1 have colluded to make unlawful gain and therefore, the petition deserves to be dismissed.

13. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner contend that the trial Court has considered the entire evidence available on record and has also bestowed NC: 2023:KHC:40585 its attention on all the points urged by the appellant/Insurance Company.
Even the evidence of the Investigating Officer was also appreciated by the Tribunal.
Therefore, he contend that there is no need for any intervention by this Court.

14. It is submitted that when the Tribunal on the basis of the appreciation of the evidence which it had recorded, has come to certain conclusion, it would not be proper on the part of the First Appellate Court to substitute its own reason unless there is glaring perversity and illegality.

Hence,
he sought for dismissal of the appeal.
15. The petitioner being a minor is represented by his guardian i.e., father.
He is examined as PW.1.
Obviously, PW.1 is not the eyewitness to the accident.

He states that when he heard the cries of his son, he rushed to the spot, found that there was an accident, wherein, the petitioner was injured and he was shifted to Aswada Hospital and thereafter to Sagar Hospital.
He states that he - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:40585 came to know that the Mahindra Pickup Goods Vehicle has caused the accident and accordingly, he lodged the complaint as per Ex.P2.

In Ex.P2, it is stated that the vehicle M/S Tata Aig General Insurance vs Master Chandan on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178577453/
4 bearing registration No.KA-08-6167 caused the accident by colliding with his son who was standing in front of the gate of his house.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the complaint, it is stated that after the accident, the driver of the vehicle had left the vehicle at the spot and the name of the driver is not known and investigation be conducted.
The accident had occurred on 18.02.2015 at about 07.00 pm and the complaint was lodged on 20.02.2015 at about 09.30 am.
There is no reason mentioned regarding the delay in filing the complaint.
16. On the same day, the Police also recorded the statement of the injured as per Ex.P2, who also has stated as mentioned in the complaint.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed the charge sheet as per Ex.P4 against the driver-cum-owner of the goods vehicle i.e.,
respondent No.1.
In the cross- - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:40585 examination of PW.1, it was suggested that there was no such accident between the vehicle of respondent No.1 and the son of PW.1, which he has denied.
There is no suggestion in the cross-examination of the PW.1 that a Tractor was involved in the accident.
The suggestion that there was negligence by the injured was denied by him.
17. The PW.2 happens to be the Medical Officer who deposed about the disability of the petitioner.
In the cross- examination, it was elicited that at the time of the admission, the casualty Medical Officer has taken information from the patient.
He admits that in the emergency case sheet, there have been overwritings that the 'tractor' has been struck off and 'four wheeler' is inserted.
18. The Insurance Company has adduced the evidence of RWs.1 to 4.
RW.1 happens to be the Medico Legal Consultant of the Sagar Hospital, he produced the medico legal register at Ex.R1 and the copy of the Police - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:40585 intimation at Ex.R2.
He states that PW.1 had given information about the accident and accordingly, it was mentioned in MLC register.

It is elicited that is Doctor Sajan Arif was the author of Exs.R1 and R2.
19.
RW.2 is the Investigating Officer and he states that he had not collected the Police intimation from the Hospital and he had not come across any information about the tractor.
20. RW.3 happens to be the Traffic PSI of Madiwala who registered the FIR.
He states that he had received Police intimation from the Sagar Hospital and later, he received the complaint and after investigation, the charge sheet was filed.
There is nothing in the cross-examination which would show that his investigation is faulty.

21. The perusal of the case sheet at Ex.P19 and the discharge summary at Ex.P9 show that the petitioner had sustained the injury in RTA while standing in front of his home near Shiva Temple, at M/S Tata Aig General Insurance vs Master Chandan on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178577453/
5 about 06.30 pm on 18.02.2016 - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:40585 a four wheeler ran over his right foot.

entities.text: Tata Aig General Insurance vs Master Chandan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The case sheet at Ex.P19 shows that it was a tractor which run over the right foot of the injured.
The word 'a tractor' was struck off and 'four wheeler' was inserted in a different ink.
In the entire P19, such corrections are made.

22. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant has placed reliance on the decision of this Court in the case of ST DEEPU Vs. THE NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND ANOTHER1 by this Court to contend that there is thick cloud of doubt about the alleged involvement of the vehicle insured by the appellant.

entities.text: ST DEEPU Vs. THE NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is to be noted that in the above cited decision,
the complaint was lodged after a delay of about a month.
No mention of the lorry details in the complaint.
The owner of the vehicle had not contested the matter, there was no explanation for delay.
Therefore, this Court held that the accident is not probabilized by the evidentiary material on record even going by the rule of preponderance of probability.
In the case on hand, the complaint was lodged on the third day of the accident and injured was a minor.
There was a clear mention about the accident involving a vehicle in the medico legal register as well as the complaint.
Therefore, the question is whether it was a tractor or it was the vehicle owned by the respondent No.1.
Therefore, on facts, the above case can be distinguished.

24. He also relied on the decision of this Court in the case of M.S.NINGEGOWDA VS. TATA AIG GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND ANOTHER2, wherein this Court had confirmed the dismissal of the claim petition on the ground that there was discrepancy in the oral evidence and also the manner in which the accident happened.

entities.text: M.S.NINGEGOWDA VS. TATA AIG GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND ANOTHER2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This court came to conclusion that the finding of the Tribunal that it was self fall from the bike but not a hit by the bike is justifiable on the basis of the entries in the Medico Legal Register.

In the case on hand, there is no such discrepancy in the oral testimony and the only discrepancy is that the MLC register initially mentioned a tractor was involved and later it was corrected as a four wheeler.

26. The Tribunal after the thorough discussion of the oral evidence and perusal of documentary evidence, came to the conclusion that the involvement of the vehicle owned by respondent No.1 is not rebutted.

It also came to conclusion that the involvement of the tractor was not probabilized by M/S Tata Aig General Insurance vs Master Chandan on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178577453/
6 the respondent No.2/appellant.

entities.text: M/S Tata Aig General Insurance vs Master Chandan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is evident from the records that initially the case sheet and the MLC register extract recorded as a accident by a tractor.
Subsequently, it was rectified as a four wheeler.
The evidence on record also show that the respondent No.1 had abandoned the vehicle at the spot and had run away.
This evidence is not found to be incorrect.
Obviously the respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence though he has filed his written statement denying any negligence on - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:40585 his part.
Under these circumstances, the conclusion reached by the Tribunal that there was an accident involving the vehicle owned by respondent No.1 is based on the evidence available on record.
The preponderance of probabilities which lean in favour of the claimant is not rebutted by the respondent.
The single ground urged by respondent is that there was correction in MLC register and the case sheet.
The said Doctor Sajan Arif has not been examined.
Obviously, the injured was a minor and he was admitted to the hospital by PW.1, who later gave complaint to the Police.
Therefore, the conclusions reached by the Tribunal cannot be held to be perverse or arbitrary.
If the two views are permissible, the view taken by the Tribunal has to be upheld, for, it had the advantage of appreciating the demeanor of the witnesses.
Therefore, I am unable to accept the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant.
The quantum of the compensation amount is not urged.
Under these circumstances, the appeal is devoid of merits.

Hence, the following;
ORDER
The appeal is dismissed.
Amount in deposit if any shall be transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith.
